faqs.q: How much does a Basenji cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $500–$2,000 for a Basenji puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Basenji?
faqs.a: Budget $120–$200 per month for a Basenji, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Small breeds often cost less on food and some products, but vet bills don't proportionally reduce — procedures cost similar amounts regardless of size.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Basenji?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($300–600), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Basenji cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Basenji are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $1,500–$3,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Basenji?
faqs.a: Basenjis need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Basenjis shed a lot?
faqs.a: Basenjis shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Basenji need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Basenji's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Basenji?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Basenjis that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis easy to train?
faqs.a: Basenjis are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Basenji?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Basenjis. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Basenji?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Basenji?
faqs.a: Basenjis can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Basenjis commonly have?
faqs.a: Basenjis are most commonly associated with kidney and other breed-specific conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Basenjis live?
faqs.a: Basenjis have an average lifespan of 13–14 years. Small breeds often live longer than large breeds. Dental care is particularly important for small dogs, as dental disease is a common longevity issue.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Basenjis than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Basenji at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Basenji puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Basenji puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Basenji-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis good with kids?
faqs.a: Basenjis can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Basenjis get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Basenjis can be selective with other dogs due to their independent nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Basenjis bark a lot?
faqs.a: Basenjis tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Basenjis adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their compact nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Basenji need per day?
faqs.a: Basenjis need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Basenjis make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Basenji doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Basenjis often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Basenji be off-lead?
faqs.a: Basenjis can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Basenji?
faqs.a: A Basenji needs approximately ½–1½ cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Basenji?
faqs.a: Adult Basenjis should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Basenji?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Basenjis benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Basenji from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Small breeds typically transition to adult food around 12 months. Moving too late keeps them on higher-calorie puppy formulas that can cause weight gain in lower-activity adults.

faqs.q: Is a Basenji a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Basenjis can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Basenjis good family dogs?
faqs.a: Basenjis can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Basenjis do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Basenjis are more independent than many breeds and generally tolerate alone time better than highly social dogs. Still, aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone for an adult dog, and less for puppies.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Basenji?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Basenji — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
